rationale.conceptual: Uses well-known computational materials science methods: CSL construction, rigid-body translation search, grain boundary energy calculation, surface energy slab model, and Mott-Littleton saddle-point search—all standard in the field. No novel derivation; just applying existing code and a published potential.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: validate potential, validate bulk barriers, construct bicrystal, run >200 energy minimizations in a translation search, compute grain boundary and surface energies, then compute migration barriers for multiple distances and mechanisms. Requires orchestrating many GULP runs, extracting results, and formatting into JSON and CSV.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces a classical atomistic simulation study of a LiCoO2 twin boundary using established methods (GULP, two-body potentials, Mott-Littleton method). The conceptual challenge is standard application of known techniques, not a new algorithm. Execution involves a multi-stage pipeline with several load-bearing steps and output formatting, but no exotic dependencies.
